rows.what: One page at /projects lists every project the member may see under a header with the title, a project count and New Project.
rows.v2: Rail › Projects (/projects)

rows.what: Counts every project not Closed (Drafts included); shown to owners only; not pressable.
rows.v2: Projects › tiles › In progress
rows.how: Counts only projects In progress, is shown to every member, and pressing it filters the list to that scope.

rows.what: Sums the contract value of every non-closed project (falling back to the typed budget), owners only, the full figure in a tooltip.
rows.v2: Projects › tiles › Contract value (Open projects)
rows.how: Shown to Owners and Admins; sums the open projects’ contract value (the signed quote, else the agreed value) with no budget estimate mixed in.

rows.feature: Tiles: Avg. Health and At Risk (health score)

rows.how: No health score. The Needs attention tile counts projects with a named reason (overdue tasks, milestones or payments, a client concern, no update for 14 days, a stalled set-up…) and filters to them.

rows.feature: Stage chips: All · Draft · Active · Closed
rows.what: Single-choice chips with counts filter the list by stage group; counts ignore the search.
rows.v2: Projects › scope pill (Open projects · All projects · Mine · To do · Setting up · In progress · Completed · On hold)
rows.how: A scope pill with counts replaces the chips; the default Open hides Completed until asked; it adds Mine and to-do scopes (Needs attention, Waiting on client, Completing this month, Needs my review); the pill’s count follows search and filters.

rows.what: Filters the list as you type, by project name or client name only.
rows.v2: Projects › toolbar › Search project, client, number…
rows.how: Also matches the number, property, property type, project type, stage, members and phone.

rows.feature: Filter by project type or team member
rows.what: No filter beyond the stage chips and the search; type and designer could only be sorted.
rows.v2: Projects › Filters (Sort · Project type · Team), applied live
rows.how: A Filters panel adds Project type and Team filters and a sort order (Newest, Oldest, Target end, Name).

rows.feature: The list keeps its view when you come back
rows.what: Nothing is kept: leaving the page and pressing Back always lands on All, table view, unsorted, at the top.
rows.v2: Projects › the address (?scope= ?q= ?sort= ?type= ?team= ?col= ?view=)
rows.how: Scope, search, Filters, sort and the view live in the address, so Back returns to the same list; the chosen view is also remembered per browser.

rows.feature: Project column (client name and property line)
rows.what: Shows the client’s name (the project name only as a fallback) over ‘property type · address’, and sorts by the hidden project name.
rows.v2: Projects › table › Project
rows.how: Shows the project’s own name over client · property, with its first attention reason (or ‘On hold till …’) underneath, and sorts by the name it shows.

rows.what: A sortable chip column with the project type.
rows.v2: Projects › Column settings › Project type (off by default)
rows.how: The column exists but is hidden until a studio turns it on, and its head does not sort; filtering by type lives in Filters.

rows.what: Shows a stored progress % that nothing in the app updates (0 at creation, only the AI tool writes it).
rows.v2: Projects › table › Progress · Next milestone
rows.how: Worked out from the schedule (milestones done of all, e.g. ‘3 of 7’), so the list and the project page agree; a Next milestone column shows the next one with its day count.

rows.what: Shows the first assignee’s initial and name only; sortable by that name.
rows.v2: Projects › table › Members
rows.how: Shows up to two avatars and ‘+n’ with Assign from the cell; the head does not sort (several people per cell) — filter by member instead.

rows.feature: Status column (Planning, In Progress, On Hold…)
rows.what: A badge with the project’s status word, set to Planning at creation and changed only by hand or the AI tool, so nearly every row reads Planning.
rows.v2: Projects › table › Stage (Setting up · In progress · Completed, an On hold mark)
rows.how: One stage word per project; no second status.

rows.feature: Commission Pending badge on Draft rows
rows.what: Every Draft row carries a yellow ‘Commission Pending’ badge, whatever is really missing (desktop only).
rows.how: There are no set-up gates and no commission at creation; a set-up left open shows as ‘Setting up for n days’.

rows.what: Project, Type and Designer heads cycle ascending · descending · off; otherwise newest first.
rows.v2: Projects › table heads; Filters › Sort
rows.how: Heads sort Project, Number, Stage, money, dates, Next milestone, Progress and Last update; Members and Project type are labels only; Filters › Sort sets the base order.

rows.feature: Open a project from its row
rows.what: Clicking a row or its hover arrow opens the project page.
rows.v2: Projects › row (name or Project cell)

rows.feature: Project cards on phones and tablets

rows.what: A pulsing ghost of the page while the app’s data loads.
rows.v2: Projects › loading ghost

rows.what: ‘No projects found · Try a different search or filter’ or ‘No projects in {stage}’, with no way to create one from there.

rows.feature: When the list fails to load

rows.v2: Projects › error page with Try again
rows.how: A failed page says it failed and offers Try again; it is never shown as an empty list.

rows.what: A Designer sees only projects they are assigned to — filtered in the browser, while the server sends every project (and every archived one).
rows.v2: Projects and every project page (checked on the server)
rows.how: Who sees a project is its lead’s rule (Settings › Who sees leads) plus the lead’s members, checked on the server for the list, the page and its actions.

rows.feature: Accounting-only members kept out of Projects

rows.how: 2.0 has no Accounting role yet.

rows.feature: Workload view (projects per person against capacity)

rows.how: Owners, Admins and Managers (a Manager sees their team); each person has their own capacity (studio default 4, set on Company › Members or Set capacity); plain words ‘Room for 2 more · Full · 1 over’; follows the scope, Filters and search; unassigned projects get their own row.

rows.feature: Archived chip and the Archived projects list
rows.what: An ‘Archived’ chip swaps the list for archived projects (name, client, archived date), shown to every role, Designers included.
rows.v2: Projects › scope › Completed (finished projects); ⋮ › Deleted Projects
rows.how: No Archive; finished projects are Completed and hidden from the default Open scope until asked.

rows.what: ‘Unarchive’ on an archived row returns it to the list at once (Owner or Admin on the server; refused silently for others); cancelled tasks stay cancelled.
rows.how: Nothing is archived; a deleted project comes back with Restore in Deleted Projects (Owners and Admins).

rows.feature: Sidebar and phone bar Projects item, with a count
rows.what: ‘Projects’ in the sidebar with a red badge counting Planning / Hacking / In Progress projects (hidden while on Projects); the phone bar’s Projects has no count.
rows.v1: Sidebar › Projects; phone bottom bar › Projects
rows.v2: Rail › Projects (badge); phone dock › Projects
rows.how: The badge counts projects that need attention and opens that scope.

rows.feature: Keyboard: G then P, and C to create
rows.what: G then P goes to Projects; C opens the create drawer; listed in the keyboard help.
rows.v2: Anywhere › G P; Projects › C (New project); the ? panel

rows.what: The topbar search matches loaded projects by name, client, phone, address, type and designer (top five), in the browser.
rows.v2: Rail › Search / ⌘K › Projects
rows.how: Runs on the server under Who sees leads; ‘/’ focuses the page’s own search box.

rows.what: A coach mark points at the header (‘Projects by stage… Create one from a signed lead’), once per browser.
rows.v2: Projects › first-run card (only while the studio has no projects)
rows.how: No tip once projects exist; the first-run card explains how a project begins.

rows.what: The Dashboard shows the project total and an Active / Completed bar, opening Projects.
rows.how: The Dashboard is not built.

rows.what: A project opens from the list, the Tasks page, the Dashboard, the lead drawer, Finance pipeline, the inbox, the quotes table, invoices and the assistant.

rows.feature: Prompt to create a project when a lead is Signed

rows.v1: Lead drawer › status Signed › Create Project drawer
rows.v2: Lead › Move stage › Won (the Won step creates the project)
rows.how: Moving a lead to Won creates its project in the same press — no second form — and the new project opens saying ‘Project P-… created’.

rows.feature: Create Project / Convert to Project buttons on the lead
rows.what: The lead drawer’s footer ‘Create Project’, the deal card’s ‘Create project’ and the readiness panel’s ‘Convert to Project’ open the create drawer.
rows.v1: Lead drawer › footer · deal card · readiness panel
rows.v2: Lead page › Convert to Project (opens Move stage at Won); after Won › Open project
rows.how: Convert to Project is winning the lead: it opens the Won step where the stage policy allows, else stays locked and says why.

rows.feature: Readiness checks before a lead becomes a project
rows.what: Designer assigned · Quote approved · Contract uploaded · Project type selected, each switchable per studio, each with a fix link and a dot counter.
rows.v2: Move stage › Won step (signed quote · contract · split to 100% · project type)
rows.how: The Won step asks for the signed quote, the contract, a payment split totalling 100% and the project type; there are no studio switches; a member is already required before a lead leaves New.

rows.feature: The lead’s status after it becomes a project
rows.what: The lead moves to Signed › Project started in a separate save after the project exists.
rows.v2: Lead stage Won; the lead keeps Overview, Quotes and Contracts
rows.how: The lead is Won in the same press; its Tasks, Files, Notes & Logs, Questionnaire and Activity then open on the project.

rows.what: The drawer opens pre-filled from the lead (client, phone, email, property type, district as address, area, style, project type, notes, contract name, assignees, budget = quote total) for review.
rows.v2: Move stage › Won (no form)
rows.how: There is no form: the project is the lead’s record plus the Won step’s choices, named ‘{property type} — {client}’; the client’s details stay on that one record.

rows.what: A client signing online moves the lead to Signed but creates no project and prompts no one; the studio has to notice the button.
rows.v2: Bell › A contract is signed; contract page › Move to Won
rows.how: The team is told by bell, and the signed contract offers Move to Won, which creates the project.

rows.what: A second project for the same lead is refused (409) by the app, not the database; deleting the lead leaves the project with no lead.
rows.v2: (rule) one project per lead; a lead with a live project can’t be deleted
rows.how: The database holds one project per lead (Won on such a lead opens it); deleting a lead with a live project is refused: ‘This lead has a project. Delete the project first.’

rows.feature: Link between the project and its lead
rows.what: ‘View lead’ in the project header opens the lead drawer; the lead shows ‘Go to Project’ / ‘View Project’.
rows.v1: Project header › View lead; lead › Go to Project
rows.v2: Project ⋮ › Open the lead’s record; lead page › Open project
rows.how: The lead link sits in the ⋮ and only for Won projects (a direct project has no lead page); Back names the lead when the project was opened from it.

rows.feature: The project shares the lead’s files, answers, quotes and portal
rows.what: Files, questionnaire answers, quotes, the contract file and the portal link stay on the lead and are read through the project; a changed phone is copied to every project of the lead.
rows.v1: Project › Files & Docs, questionnaire, quote list
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes; Client › Questionnaire; ⋮ › Invite to Portal

rows.feature: New Project for a client with no lead
rows.what: ‘+ New Project’ (or C) opens the create drawer with no lead, for any role; after saving it opens the new project.
rows.v2: Projects › New project (C; ⌘K › Create)

rows.what: Name (required), mobile with any country’s dial code, and email (not validated).
rows.v2: New project › Client name · Client’s phone number · Email
rows.how: The phone is required and must be a Singapore number; email is checked; a phone or email already on a lead or project asks whether to open it or create anyway.

rows.what: Property type, address, area (sqft) and style; area and style were pasted into the notes as text.
rows.v2: New project › Property type; More details › District · Property address · Floor area (sq ft) · Style

rows.what: A required project name (default ‘{property type} — {client}’) and a project type from the studio’s list or six defaults.
rows.v2: New project › Project name · Project type
rows.how: Three project types only (Whole-home renovation · Partial renovation · Commercial fit-out); the name follows client and property type until typed; a name another project uses is refused.

rows.what: Twelve room chips (Living Room … Others) saved as the project’s scope.
rows.v2: New project › More details › Rooms in the scope; ⋮ › Edit details

rows.feature: Budget and quote total on creation
rows.what: An optional Budget (may be empty or zero); a converted lead shows the signed quote’s final total read-only.
rows.v1: Create Project drawer › Budget · Quote total
rows.v2: New project › Agreed value (S$); a Won project’s value is its signed quote
rows.how: A direct project needs an agreed value above zero (GST included); a Won project’s contract value is the signed quote or the uploaded quote’s amount; no separate budget.

rows.what: A designer picker showing ‘{specialty} · {n} active’; several designers with even commission splits; defaults to the lead’s assignees or the creating designer.
rows.v2: New project › Members (specialty · n projects running, a suggestion)
rows.how: No commission split here (it lives in Finance › Commission); a Designer’s own project is locked to them; a Won project’s members are its lead’s.

rows.feature: Start and target dates on creation

rows.v2: Project › Start the project sheet (Works start on); Needs you › Target end date
rows.how: Dates aren’t asked at creation: Start the project asks when works start, the target end comes from the schedule or its own dialog, and a start after the target end is refused.

rows.what: Shows the quote’s schedule read-only, or editable stages (name, %, trigger, add/remove, must total 100%) defaulting to the studio template or 10/30/30/30.

rows.what: Use studio default · set a custom rate (owner) or request one (designer, leaving the project in Draft until approved) · skip; flat or per milestone.
rows.v2: Company › Finance › Commission (the studio rule, a project’s or member’s rate, asks, the team’s shares)
rows.how: Nothing about commission is asked at creation; the studio’s rule applies and a project or member rate, an ask and the team’s shares are set in Finance; commission never holds a project back.

rows.feature: Floor plan and signed contract on creation

rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files (starter folders); Needs you › Contract
rows.how: Files are uploaded for real once the project exists (starter folders Contract & VOs, Floor plans, Renders, Quotes & BOQ, Site photos); the Won step’s contract becomes a contract record; a direct project adds its contract from the Contract step.

rows.what: A notes box saved as the project’s notes.
rows.v2: New project › More details › A first note
rows.how: The note becomes the first entry in the project’s Notes & Logs.

rows.what: Required fields and 100% splits, an error summary and a shaking ‘Fix Errors to Save’, a ‘Defaults Applied’ confirm dialog, then a chain of saves with partial-failure toasts.
rows.v1: Create Project drawer › footer · confirm dialog
rows.v2: New project › Create
rows.how: House form: errors after the first press, cleared as fixed; no confirm step; one save writes the client’s record, team, questions, first note and project together; ‘Project P-… created’ and the project opens.

rows.feature: A hidden client record for a no-lead project

rows.v2: (system) a direct lead, never shown in Leads
rows.how: The client’s record is a ‘direct’ lead kept out of the Leads pipeline; its lead pages redirect to the project, so every edit happens on the project.

rows.feature: Draft invoices made with the project

rows.v2: Project › Money (one draft per payment stage)

rows.what: An orphan page at /projects/new (name, client, property type, budget defaulting to 50,000, ‘Dec 2024’ target, Planning/In Progress chips), reachable only by typing its address.
rows.v2: Projects › New project
rows.how: One New project form; no separate page.

rows.what: A dialog (same, another or a new customer) and a route copying a project’s details, timeline and quote snapshot into a new Draft — nothing in 1.0 opened it.

rows.how: Suggestions are scripted and act only through the project’s own actions and rules; nothing sets a stage, status or progress directly.

rows.feature: Draft stage and its five set-up checks

rows.how: Guidance, not gates: each item has its own button; commission is not one of them; what the Start sheet asks itself is left off the list.

rows.what: A stepped dialog over the open checks (designer, quote, contract, payment schedule, commission) whose last step makes the project Active even if steps were skipped.

rows.v2: Each Before work starts row’s own button; Stage ▾ › In progress (Start the project)

rows.v2: Stage ▾ › In progress / the header’s Start the project → Start sheet
rows.how: One press by the project’s team, Managers, Owners or Admins: asks when works start and can set up the schedule, invite the client and send the deposit invoice in the same sheet; refused while on hold or after the target end.

rows.what: Raising invoices, variation orders and POs and completing milestones are refused while Draft (‘Financial actions are restricted…’); expenses still allowed.

rows.what: A per-studio running number shown as ‘#31’ before the name; taken before the insert, so a failure leaves a gap.

rows.what: Region lists (Singapore’s eighteen, plus Malaysia, UAE and India); the edit card used its own fixed Singapore list.
rows.v1: Create drawer › Property Type; Property card
rows.v2: New project / Edit details › Property type
rows.how: Singapore’s list only, the same one leads use.

notes: Read from code on both sides: 1.0 at qanvast-id-tool @ 620190192, 2.0 as the working tree stands on 2026-10-10 (after the simplify build). 1.0 pieces that nothing could open were left out as rows and are noted here: project-card.tsx, project-card-updated.tsx, SetupProgressIndicator, usePortfolioKPIs, the unreachable Quick Actions menu and legacy sidebar, the project_templates store (two APIs, no screen), the retired payment-schedule rebalance route, the unused action-items fetch, the never-opened Financial Report / Credit Note / Invoice Editor dialogs and the hidden ?tab=render body; layout, motion and the docs-versus-code rows (A-07…A-18, A-71…A-80, A-216…A-223, B-335…B-345, D-349…D-357, K) are not product features. The first schedule (B §6), money detail, updates and the portal set-up are other readers’ areas and appear here only where the Overview or the frame shows them. One 2.0 drift worth knowing: the gaps build put Put on hold / Resume on the listing’s row menu, but the parity build moved stage moves to the project page’s Stage ▾, so a hold can no longer be set from the list. Per-project currency (1.0 formatted by the project’s country) was not mapped here; 2.0 prints S$ only.
